name: Bosch EDC15P / EDC15P+ / EDC15V (VAG 1.9 TDI)
cpu: C167 family (Bosch-marked, e.g. B59388 on EDC15P+)

read_methods.notes: Programmed over K-line, without CAN (ecupinouts); the same K-line is on the OBD socket, so OBD and bench use the same protocol. The 121-pin connector also carries a powertrain CAN pair that Diag-Prof marks as not used for diagnostics. A board-level boot mode exists for recovery (obdii365 article).

notes: Classic VAG TDI diesel ECU: EDC15V on the rotary-pump (VP37) 1.9 TDI, EDC15P/P+ on the unit-injector (PD) 1.9 TDI. Part numbers above are VAG prefixes (028906021xx / 038906019xx), not single software keys. OpenTune's edc15 checksum (alias of edc15c6) fully solves the VAG TDI 512 KiB layout and self-corrects.

connectors.name: T121
connectors.description: 121-pin Bosch connector (81 vehicle-side + 40 engine-side). Diag-Prof labels the vehicle block T81; pin numbers are the same.

bench.notes: K-line only: +12 V to pins 37 (terminal 30) and 2 (terminal 15), ground on 4 and 5, K-line on 16. Diag-Prof also lists pin 1 as terminal 15; feeding it too is harmless per that source.
bench.resistor_notes: No CAN termination needed: diagnostics and programming run over K-line.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.

sources.title: Diag-Prof: VAG Bosch EDC15P / EDC15P+ (pin assignment, memory)
obdii365: reading VAG Bosch EDC15P/EDC15P+ in boot mode
OpenTune vehicle catalog (catalog/manual, engine to ECU-family mapping)
fjvva/ecu-tool, EDC15 User Manual (project licence unspecified)
Dilemma (author), VAG EDC15P hardware and communication notes, in the author's VAGEDCSuite repository (licence unspecified)

obd.notes: ecu-tool documents a full flash read and writes to the calibration area through the vehicle socket on supported EDC15P, EDC15V and 512 KiB EDC15VM units. Its manual excludes the 1 MiB EDC15VM.

bench.how: On T121, apply +12 V to pins 2 and 37, ground pins 4 and 5, and use pin 16 for K-line diagnostics. Pins 6 (CAN-L) and 7 (CAN-H) carry powertrain CAN. Diag-Prof labels 2 as switched and 37 as permanent. Dilemma labels 37 as switched, so confirm the ignition feed for the specific revision.

boot.mcu_mode: C167 bootstrap mode on the documented EDC15P board.
boot.reset_timing: DQ4 is sampled low at startup. The source gives no release interval.
boot.notes: Dilemma identifies DQ4 on the EDC15P flash chip as the boot input. The board connection on other revisions is unconfirmed.

security.notes: The ecu-tool manual mentions authentication during model selection. It does not establish the access requirement for a complete diagnostic read or for programming across these revisions. OpenTune ships no OEM key.

flash_note: The documented EDC15P has a 512 KiB Am29F400. The ecu-tool manual distinguishes 512 KiB and 1 MiB EDC15VM revisions.
